summary: Regime read: Potential pivot → tightening. Of the weighted evidence, 32% points tightening, 56% mixed, and 12% easing. Inflation is strongly tightening (per Yahoo Finance: Hot CPI Print Shakes Fed Cut Bets as Inflation Tops ). Fed communications are strongly tightening (per CNBC: Fed meeting recap: July 2026). Employment is strongly easing and market pricing is strongly tightening.
what_would_change_the_call: A second consecutive upside inflation surprise.
Front-end (2Y) yields rising materially further over the intermeeting window.
A Fed official explicitly pushing back against near-term cuts.
Fed funds futures repricing from 'fewer cuts' toward outright hikes.

checklist.text: Fed communications explicitly de-emphasize further easing
Fed emphasizes inflation upside risks over labor weakness
Market pricing removes expected cuts or starts pricing hikes
2Y yields rise materially over the intermeeting window
Inflation data surprises to the upside
Employment remains firm enough to reduce pressure for cuts
SPY/TLT color and rate-market behavior confirm the macro read

scoring.method: weighted vote-share over source direction, one vote per event cluster (no magnitude averaging)
scoring.clustering: one vote per event_key; representative = max-weight source; keyless sources are singleton clusters

sources.title: How Can Employment Data Impact Fed Policy?
sources.evidence_text: August jobs report showed 142,000 additions and unemployment edged lower to 4.2%, supporting the view that the labor market is cooling.
sources.why_it_matters: Cooling labor data influenced the Fed's September decision to cut rates by 0.50%, illustrating the direct policy link.

sources.title: June PCE Report: PCE Inflation Index Up 2.6%, Stronger Than Expected
sources.evidence_text: Morningstar reported June PCE at 2.6% year over year and core PCE at 2.8% year over year, both above expectations.
sources.why_it_matters: An upside surprise in the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge makes faster policy easing less likely.

sources.title: US labor market stays afloat as unemployment rate falls to 4.2%
sources.evidence_text: The August employment report showed the unemployment rate falling to 4.2% and wages still rising robustly.
sources.why_it_matters: A lower unemployment rate and firm wage growth reduce the urgency for near-term Fed cuts and argue against rate hikes only if inflation stays contained.

sources.title: Meeting calendars and information
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve publishes the FOMC meeting calendar and related meeting information on its official site.
sources.why_it_matters: The calendar anchors the next policy decision date and frames the timing of any cut or hike expectations.

sources.title: US labor market adds 73,000 jobs in July while May, June reports see 'larger than normal' downward revisions
sources.evidence_text: The July jobs report was described as a miss on payrolls with upward pressure on unemployment expectations and a sharp increase in market odds of a September Fed cut.
sources.why_it_matters: Market repricing toward cuts signals that investors think the Fed's employment mandate is weakening relative to inflation concerns.

sources.title: Why a CPI surprise could trip up the Fed's rate-cutting plans
sources.evidence_text: The article says an upside CPI surprise could push the Fed toward a pause in rate cuts and keep the policy rate unchanged at the next meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: If inflation surprises higher, the Fed is more likely to delay easing to preserve credibility on price stability.

sources.title: Inflation edges up, highlighting Fed's bumpy path to stable prices
sources.evidence_text: The article says October CPI rose to 2.6% year over year, which it described as a bump that still likely would not change the Fed's near-term course.
sources.why_it_matters: A firmer inflation print reduces the Fed's room to cut aggressively even if it does not fully reverse the easing cycle.

sources.title: Monetary Policy and the Fed's Framework Review
sources.evidence_text: Powell said policy was already much closer to neutral than a year earlier and that labor-market stability allowed the Fed to proceed carefully with further changes.
sources.why_it_matters: A closer-to-neutral stance and stable employment tend to keep the door open to additional easing if inflation cooperates.

sources.title: US Jobs Fall Unexpectedly, Complicating Fed's Next Rate ...
sources.evidence_text: The report framed the latest unemployment decline as partly driven by a lower labor-force participation rate rather than stronger hiring.
sources.why_it_matters: A participation-driven unemployment move is less inflationary than broad hiring strength, which modestly supports easier policy.

sources.title: FedWatch - CME Group
sources.evidence_text: CME's FedWatch tool uses 30-Day Fed Funds futures prices to track the probabilities of Fed rate changes implied by market pricing.
sources.why_it_matters: This is the primary market-based gauge for whether traders are leaning toward additional cuts or a tighter policy path.

sources.title: Inflation (PCE)
sources.evidence_text: The Fed states that it seeks 2 percent inflation over the longer run as measured by the annual change in the PCE price index.
sources.why_it_matters: Any PCE reading materially above 2 percent implies less room for easing under the Fed’s price-stability mandate.

sources.title: Trimmed Mean PCE inflation rate
sources.evidence_text: The Dallas Fed’s trimmed mean PCE inflation rate was 2.4 percent over the 12 months ending in May, while headline PCE was 4.1 percent and core PCE was 3.4 percent.
sources.why_it_matters: A trimmed-mean measure above 2 percent suggests underlying inflation is still sticky, which argues for caution on rate cuts.

sources.title: Personal Consumption Expenditures: Chain-type Price Index
sources.evidence_text: FRED shows the PCE price index at 131.527 in May 2026, indicating the latest available monthly reading in the series is still elevated.
sources.why_it_matters: A still-rising PCE series reinforces that inflation is not yet back at target, limiting the Fed’s room to ease.

sources.title: Monetary Policy Report, July 2026
sources.evidence_text: The Fed said core PCE inflation was 3.4% over the 12 months ending in May, with housing services up 3.2% and core nonhousing services up 3.9%.
sources.why_it_matters: Sticky core and services inflation reduces the Fed's confidence that inflation is moving sustainably to 2%, which argues against rapid cuts.

sources.title: Macro in a Minute: Inflation, Jobs, and the Fed
sources.evidence_text: The piece says stronger-than-expected inflation data led markets to align with the Fed's projected 75 basis points of cuts rather than pricing a more aggressive easing path.
sources.why_it_matters: When markets reprice toward fewer cuts, financial conditions tighten and the Fed sees less support for easing from market expectations.

sources.title: Fed rate cut unlikely; would be 'like throwing oil on the fire' of ...
sources.evidence_text: Commentary cited outside experts arguing that the Fed is unlikely to cut rates at the upcoming meeting and that a hike case is stronger than a cut case.
sources.why_it_matters: If market and analyst expectations shift toward no cuts or hikes, the Fed gets less room to ease without surprising financial conditions.

sources.title: 30 Day Federal Funds Futures Overview
sources.evidence_text: CME says FedWatch is built from 30-Day Fed Funds futures and is used to gauge the probability of an upcoming rate hike.
sources.why_it_matters: Because futures prices embed expected policy rates, a shift in those prices can indicate whether the market expects the Fed to ease or tighten.

sources.title: Fed Rate Monitor
sources.evidence_text: The market-implied next meeting outcome shown is a 25 bp hike, with the tool also displaying two hikes by year-end.
sources.why_it_matters: If futures and related pricing lean toward hikes, the market is assigning higher odds to a restrictive Fed path rather than cuts.

sources.title: Fed Decision in July? Trading Odds & Predictions 2026
sources.evidence_text: The event page says market-implied odds favor no change at 79.5%, with 19.4% pricing for a 25 bp hike and negligible cut odds.
sources.why_it_matters: If market participants mostly price a hold but still assign meaningful hike odds, the reaction function is being pulled toward tighter policy rather than easing.

sources.title: Federal Reserve: Extended pause guidance – UOB
sources.publisher: Mitrade / UOB Global Economics & Markets Research
sources.evidence_text: The note says the Fed is widely expected to keep the policy rate unchanged at the July meeting and that OIS swaps price roughly a one-third probability of a 25bp hike.
sources.why_it_matters: A meaningful hike probability in OIS indicates markets are assigning nontrivial odds to tighter policy rather than further easing.

sources.title: What's The Fed's Next Move?
sources.evidence_text: J.P. Morgan said it expected the Fed to stay on hold through the rest of 2026 and did not expect the first hike until September 2027.
sources.why_it_matters: A hold-then-hike forecast implies the Fed reaction function is still weighted toward inflation persistence rather than immediate easing.

sources.title: US 2 Year Treasury Bond Note Yield - Quote - Chart
sources.evidence_text: Trading Economics shows the U.S. 2-year Treasury yield around 4.12% and forecasts 3.92% in 12 months.
sources.why_it_matters: A lower expected 2-year yield over the next year implies markets see policy easing relative to today, but the near-term level still signals restrictive policy expectations.

sources.title: The Fed’s Favorite Measure Of Inflation Cooled Down In June
sources.evidence_text: The June PCE report showed headline inflation at 3.7% year over year and core PCE at 3.3%, both below the prior month.
sources.why_it_matters: Cooling inflation eases pressure on the Fed and modestly improves the case for eventual cuts, though levels remain above target.

sources.title: Survey of Consumer Expectations
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
sources.evidence_text: The New York Fed's Survey of Consumer Expectations is a recurring household survey used to track inflation expectations.
sources.why_it_matters: Inflation expectations matter because the Fed watches whether longer-run expectations remain anchored when deciding how much tightening or easing is still needed.

sources.title: August 2026 CPI release
sources.evidence_text: The latest CPI release showed consumer price inflation remains above the Fed’s 2% objective, limiting room for near-term easing.
sources.why_it_matters: A CPI reading above target reduces the Fed’s confidence that inflation is moving sustainably to 2%, which argues for fewer cuts.

sources.title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC kept the federal funds target range at 3.50% to 3.75% while saying inflation remains elevated and three voters preferred a 25 basis point hike.
sources.why_it_matters: A hold with dissent toward a hike signals a less easing-friendly reaction function and raises the bar for cuts.

sources.title: Statement on My FOMC Dissent
sources.evidence_text: A Minneapolis Fed policymaker said she dissented because she preferred to raise the federal funds target range by 0.25 percentage point this week.
sources.why_it_matters: An explicit rate-hike dissent indicates concern that inflation or other conditions warrant tighter policy than the majority chose.

sources.title: Fed meeting recap: July 2026
sources.evidence_text: The Fed kept rates at 3.50% to 3.75% at the July meeting, and the press conference emphasized meeting the 2% inflation goal.
sources.why_it_matters: Holding rates steady while stressing the inflation objective suggests the reaction function is still biased toward fewer cuts and potentially tighter policy if inflation persists.

sources.title: Transcript of Chairman Warsh's Press Conference -- July 29, 2026
sources.evidence_text: The July FOMC left the policy rate unchanged at 3.50% to 3.75% in a 9-3 vote, while stating that job gains have kept pace with the workforce and inflation remains elevated relative to the 2% goal.
sources.why_it_matters: A hold with elevated inflation language and three hike dissents points to a less-dovish reaction function and reduces the odds of near-term cuts.

sources.title: Monetary Policy
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve states that monetary policy is aimed at maximum employment, stable prices, and moderate long-term interest rates.
sources.why_it_matters: This frames the reaction function that any employment or inflation data must be judged against.

sources.title: H.15 - Selected Interest Rates (Daily) - August 10, 2026
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve’s H.15 release shows the 2-year Treasury yield at 4.25% on August 10, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: The 2-year yield is a front-end rate that reflects how markets expect the policy path to evolve over the next several meetings.

sources.title: US weekly jobless claims increase less than expected
sources.evidence_text: Initial jobless claims rose by 9,000 to 197,000 for the week ended July 25, and continuing claims fell to 1.782 million for the prior week.
sources.why_it_matters: The report shows claims remained low enough to suggest labor market stability, which does not strongly pressure the Fed toward immediate cuts or hikes.

sources.title: Fed's Preferred Inflation Gauge Cools to 3.7%
sources.evidence_text: The June PCE inflation rate fell to 3.7% year over year and core PCE eased to 3.3%, but both remained well above 2%.
sources.why_it_matters: Cooling inflation helps the easing case, but the level remains too hot to strongly support near-term cuts.

sources.title: June 2026 PCE inflation falls 0.1%, consumer spending up 0.3%
sources.evidence_text: The BEA reported that headline PCE declined 0.1% in June while core PCE rose 0.1% on the month and 3.3% year over year.
sources.why_it_matters: The month-over-month cooling supports the case for patience, although core inflation still running above target limits how far the Fed can ease.

sources.title: July 2026 Monetary Policy Report coverage
sources.evidence_text: PIMCO said its baseline still expects the Fed to stay on hold through 2026 as inflation gradually eases.
sources.why_it_matters: A hold scenario implies inflation is not yet soft enough to justify rapid easing, but also not hot enough to force immediate tightening.

sources.title: CPI Inflation Contributions from Goods and Services
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco
sources.evidence_text: The San Francisco Fed’s inflation decomposition tool shows how goods and services contributions can be monitored to assess whether inflation pressure is broad-based or fading.
sources.why_it_matters: Broad services contribution would support a slower pace of easing because it signals persistent underlying inflation.

sources.title: Prices, Wages and Workers: The Recent U.S. Inflation Experience
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
sources.evidence_text: The St. Louis Fed reiterates that the FOMC’s price-stability goal is 2% inflation as measured by the annual change in the PCE price index.
sources.why_it_matters: Any inflation or wage signal above that benchmark reduces the Fed’s tolerance for additional easing.

sources.title: 30 Day Federal Funds Futures Quotes
sources.evidence_text: CME states that 30-day fed funds futures are used to gauge the probability of an upcoming Fed rate hike.
sources.why_it_matters: This is the primary market instrument behind FedWatch-style pricing, so it is the cleanest direct read on whether the market is pricing cuts out or hikes in.

sources.title: Treasury yields jump as traders reduce expectations for any 2026 Fed rate cuts
sources.evidence_text: MarketWatch reported that traders cut back expectations for any 2026 Fed rate cuts, with the probability of a reduction this year falling to 8.8% and even a hike entering the pricing.
sources.why_it_matters: If the market is pricing out cuts and adding hikes, financial conditions are tightening relative to the Fed's current stance.

sources.title: United States - Monthly Data
sources.evidence_text: BLS monthly data show July payroll change at -23,000, unemployment at 4.1%, and average hourly earnings at 37.62.
sources.why_it_matters: The combination of weaker job growth and only moderate wage gains points to less labor-market inflation pressure in the Fed's reaction function.

sources.title: August | 2026 - FRED Blog
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
sources.evidence_text: The FRED Blog notes that its August discussion uses monthly employment data reported by the BLS.
sources.why_it_matters: FRED commentary can help contextualize the labor trend, but the Fed reacts primarily to the underlying official data.

sources.title: PCE inflation data has finally cooled — this is what it means for advisors
sources.evidence_text: The article says June PCE cooled but should not be read as a signal that the Fed is turning dovish yet.
sources.why_it_matters: This reflects a market interpretation that softer inflation improves cut odds, while still leaving the Fed cautious.

sources.title: 5-Year, 5-Year Forward Inflation Expectation Rate (T5YIFR)
sources.evidence_text: The 5-year, 5-year forward inflation expectation rate was 2.18% on 2026-06-23.
sources.why_it_matters: Well-anchored market inflation compensation supports the case for easing if realized inflation continues to cool.

sources.title: Lower-Than-Expected Inflation Keeps Fed On Track For October Rate Cut
sources.evidence_text: The piece says September CPI rose more slowly than expected and kept the Fed on track to cut rates in October.
sources.why_it_matters: When inflation undershoots forecasts, the Fed has more room to ease without appearing to risk reaccelerating prices.

sources.title: Tame US inflation gives the Fed room for more rate cuts
sources.evidence_text: ING argued that softer November inflation gave the Fed more room to deliver additional cuts in 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: A clear disinflation surprise eases the constraint on the Fed's inflation mandate and supports more accommodation.

sources.title: The Fed - Live Video - Federal Reserve
sources.evidence_text: The Fed lists a live broadcast page that may contain this week’s public remarks or events.
sources.why_it_matters: A scheduled Fed appearance can move expectations for the policy path if it includes guidance on inflation or employment.

sources.title: Federal Reserve news and events page showing July 29 FOMC materials
sources.evidence_text: The Fed's news page lists July 29 FOMC statement and opening statement materials for that meeting date.
sources.why_it_matters: This confirms the timing of the latest official policy communication relevant to the Fed's near-term stance.

sources.title: The Fed - July 28-29, 2026 FOMC Meeting
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve posted the July 28-29 FOMC meeting press conference materials on its site, indicating the meeting event and communications release.
sources.why_it_matters: The post-meeting press conference is where the Fed usually clarifies whether inflation or labor market risks are driving the policy stance.

sources.title: CME FedWatch Tool User Guide
sources.evidence_text: CME states that FedWatch analyzes the probability of FOMC rate moves for upcoming meetings.
sources.why_it_matters: The tool directly maps futures pricing into expected policy outcomes, which is the core input for judging whether markets expect easing or tightening.

sources.title: Employment Situation Summary Table A. Household data
sources.evidence_text: BLS household data for June 2026 show the unemployment rate at 4.2%, down from 4.3% in May, with the labor force and employment both lower on the month.
sources.why_it_matters: A softer unemployment print points toward less labor-market pressure, which leans against tighter policy and modestly toward easing.

sources.title: June 2026 PCE Price Index
sources.evidence_text: The June PCE report showed headline inflation easing to 3.7% year over year and core PCE easing to 3.3% year over year.
sources.why_it_matters: Easing PCE inflation supports eventual cuts, but the level remains well above target and does not by itself justify a hawkish pivot.

sources.title: Inflation Nowcasting
sources.evidence_text: The Cleveland Fed provides daily nowcasts for PCE and CPI inflation ahead of official releases.
sources.why_it_matters: Near-term inflation nowcasts help gauge whether incoming data are likely to reinforce or weaken the case for further Fed easing.

sources.title: 2-year Treasury yield rises as traders pull back on expectations for March rate cut
sources.evidence_text: The article reports that traders scaled back March cut odds in CME FedWatch, with the 25-basis-point cut probability falling to 15.9% from 23.2%.
sources.why_it_matters: A lower cut probability means the market is pricing less easing, which is consistent with a more restrictive expected path for policy.

sources.title: FedWatch API
sources.evidence_text: CME says its FedWatch API provides access to FedWatch probabilities derived from Fed Funds futures.
sources.why_it_matters: This is the underlying market-pricing feed used to monitor whether cuts are being priced out or hikes are being priced in.

sources.title: U.S. labor market resilient despite rate hikes; housing market wilting
sources.evidence_text: Initial claims decreased by 2,000 to 250,000, while the piece frames the labor market as still tight despite slower momentum.
sources.why_it_matters: A firm claims level argues against rapid easing because the Fed can still see labor market resilience alongside inflation concerns.

sources.title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
sources.evidence_text: The June FOMC minutes say the Committee left the federal funds target range unchanged at 3.50% to 3.75% while noting PCE inflation at 3.8% and core PCE inflation at 3.3% in April.
sources.why_it_matters: A hold paired with still-elevated inflation suggests the Fed is not yet signaling imminent easing and remains attentive to its price-stability mandate.

sources.title: Elevated inflation will likely delay interest rate cuts this year, warns Federal Reserve chair Powell
sources.evidence_text: Powell said recent data had not increased confidence that inflation is under control and indicated that high inflation could push rate cuts later.
sources.why_it_matters: The Fed reaction function gives less weight to easing when officials say inflation progress is insufficient and rates may need to stay restrictive longer.

sources.title: Sticky inflation report unlikely to keep Fed off course for rate cut next week
sources.evidence_text: The story said August CPI was sticky, but most commentators still expected a 25-basis-point cut rather than a larger move.
sources.why_it_matters: A sticky but not sharply hotter inflation print tends to cap the size of easing rather than fully reverse it.

sources.title: Employment Situation Summary - 2026 M07 Results
sources.evidence_text: BLS reported that nonfarm payroll employment fell by 23,000 in July while the unemployment rate was 4.1%.
sources.why_it_matters: A softer payroll print with unemployment still contained reduces urgency for the Fed to keep policy tight and modestly supports additional easing.

sources.title: US labor market stable; worker productivity accelerates in second ...
sources.evidence_text: Initial claims rose 1,000 to 199,000 for the week ended August 1, remaining below economists' forecasts and consistent with a stable labor market.
sources.why_it_matters: A stable claims print does not materially intensify recession risk, so it neither strongly pushes the Fed toward cuts nor toward hikes.

sources.title: CPI rose 2.8 percent over 12 months in July 2026
sources.evidence_text: The Bureau of Labor Statistics scheduled the July CPI release for mid-August, which is the key official inflation print after the late-July labor data in the prompt.
sources.why_it_matters: If inflation re-accelerates, the Fed has less room to respond to softer labor data with cuts.

sources.title: June 2026 Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index, excluding food and energy
sources.evidence_text: BEA reported core PCE inflation at 3.3% year over year in June 2026, down from 3.4% in May.
sources.why_it_matters: A modest cooling in the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge supports the case for eventual easing, though the level remains above target.

sources.title: US PCE Inflation Cools as Core Gauge Falls to 3.3%, Easing Fed Policy Pressure
sources.evidence_text: TradingKey reported that June headline PCE slowed to 3.7 percent year over year and core PCE eased to 3.3 percent.
sources.why_it_matters: A cooler PCE print modestly improves the case for cuts by reducing near-term inflation pressure, though inflation is still well above target.

sources.title: Fed’s favored inflation gauge shows prices edged down in June but remain high
sources.evidence_text: Yahoo Finance reported that June PCE fell 0.1% month over month, while year-over-year PCE remained 3.7% and core PCE 3.3%.
sources.why_it_matters: The monthly cooling is somewhat easier for the Fed, but the still-elevated core rate keeps inflation pressure from fully supporting cuts.

sources.title: Speech by Governor Miran on the inflation outlook
sources.evidence_text: Governor Miran said services inflation was moving sideways and that market-based core inflation excluding shelter was running below 2.3%, near target.
sources.why_it_matters: A Fed official highlighting subdued ex-shelter inflation supports the view that underlying inflation may be close enough to target to permit cuts.

sources.title: What is keeping core inflation above 2 percent?
sources.evidence_text: The Dallas Fed said core PCE was expected to be 2.9% in August 2025 and had stayed above 2.5% since mid-2024.
sources.why_it_matters: Persistently elevated core PCE suggests inflation is still above target, which supports a cautious Fed stance.

sources.title: August 2026 Rates Recap
sources.evidence_text: CME said FedWatch shows markets pricing in just one rate hike for the rest of 2026, down from two before the July 29 Fed meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: If traders are pricing fewer cuts and even a hike, the market is signaling a more restrictive policy path than the Fed’s current stance.

sources.title: Federal Reserve: Extended pause guidance
sources.evidence_text: UOB said the Fed was widely expected to hold rates steady, while OIS swaps still priced roughly a one-third chance of a 25 bp hike at the July meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: A meaningful hike probability implies markets were leaning toward a more restrictive Fed reaction function than an easing one.

sources.title: STIR: Market As Confident Of A May Hike As It Was Ahead Previous Hike
sources.evidence_text: The piece argues that STIR markets were pricing a hike with unusually high confidence relative to prior hike episodes.
sources.why_it_matters: A market that leans toward a hike indicates the reaction function is being read as more inflation-sensitive and less supportive of cuts.

sources.title: Market Yield on U.S. Treasury Securities at 2-Year Constant Maturity
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)
sources.evidence_text: The 2-year Treasury yield was 4.20% on 2026-08-12, showing front-end rates remained elevated even after recent market moves.
sources.why_it_matters: The 2-year yield is a key market gauge of expected Fed policy over the next 12 to 24 months, so its level helps infer whether pricing leans toward cuts or fewer cuts.

sources.title: Treasury Yield Premiums
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco
sources.evidence_text: The San Francisco Fed estimated the 2-year Treasury's average expected overnight rate at 3.9% versus an observed yield of 4.13% on 2026-08-12.
sources.why_it_matters: This decomposition links the 2-year yield to expected overnight rates, making it a direct read on the market's expected Fed path.

sources.title: Rate Expectations (2Y − Fed Funds): Chart, Current Level and Historical Data
sources.evidence_text: The 2-year Treasury yield minus the effective federal funds rate was 0.59 percentage points on 2026-08-11.
sources.why_it_matters: A positive spread indicates the market expects policy to stay above current overnight rates, which is more consistent with fewer cuts than with aggressive easing.

sources.title: United States Initial Jobless Claims
sources.evidence_text: Trading Economics described the latest claims reading as consistent with a strong labor market near recent lows.
sources.why_it_matters: A strong labor market reduces the urgency for Fed cuts and is more consistent with keeping policy restrictive for longer.

sources.title: Monetary Policy Report
sources.evidence_text: The Fed said inflation had risen this year, remained above its 2 percent objective, and noted that total PCE inflation was 4.1 percent over the 12 months ending in May while core PCE was 3.4 percent.
sources.why_it_matters: Persistent inflation above target argues for fewer cuts and keeps the Fed focused on restoring price stability before easing further.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Board - 2026 FOMC Press Releases
sources.evidence_text: The Fed released the July FOMC decision page for the meeting in which the Committee maintained the federal funds target range at 3.5 percent to 3.75 percent.
sources.why_it_matters: Holding rates steady while inflation is still above target signals no urgency to ease and preserves tightening risk if data do not improve.

sources.title: Market Probability Tracker
sources.evidence_text: The Atlanta Fed offers a market probability tracker that estimates policy-rate odds from market prices.
sources.why_it_matters: A Fed-owned market-pricing tracker is useful for cross-checking whether futures are assigning more weight to cuts or hikes.

sources.title: Fed Preview: Next Man Up
sources.evidence_text: The preview says the Fed is expected to hold rates steady and that the key risk is removing its easing bias rather than signaling an imminent hike.
sources.why_it_matters: A hold with a fading easing bias suggests policy is not actively easing, but it also does not yet confirm renewed tightening.

sources.title: 2-Year Treasury Yield: Federal Reserve Policy Expectations
sources.evidence_text: The source frames the 2-year Treasury yield as a proxy for expected Fed policy over the next 12 to 24 months.
sources.why_it_matters: This is a general interpretation tool rather than a fresh market release, so it adds little direct evidence on the current easing-tightening balance.

sources.title: Shock Drop in US Payrolls Eases Pressure on Fed to Hike
sources.evidence_text: Bloomberg reported that July payrolls fell unexpectedly, prior months were revised lower, and wage growth slowed to its weakest pace in nearly five years.
sources.why_it_matters: The combination of weaker hiring, revisions, and slower wages supports a more dovish Fed reaction function.

sources.title: FOMC statement
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC kept the federal funds target range unchanged at its August 6 meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: A hold signal means the Fed is not yet responding to labor cooling with immediate cuts, keeping policy data-dependent.

sources.title: VIEW Soft July jobs report fuels skepticism over possible Fed rate hike
sources.evidence_text: Reuters said July payrolls fell by 23,000, June was revised to a smaller gain, and the unemployment rate slipped to 4.1% as participation declined.
sources.why_it_matters: Markets and policymakers tend to read weaker payrolls and downward revisions as reducing the odds of near-term Fed tightening.

sources.title: Hot CPI Print Shakes Fed Cut Bets as Inflation Tops ...
sources.evidence_text: A hotter-than-expected July CPI release pushed market pricing away from near-term Fed cuts.
sources.why_it_matters: An upside inflation surprise reduces confidence that inflation is on a clean path to 2%, which argues for fewer or later cuts.

sources.title: The Federal Reserve, Economic Outlook and Monetary Policy
sources.evidence_text: The Kansas City Fed posted a speech page for an outlook-and-policy address tied to the July 2026 period, but the provided excerpt does not include substantive policy guidance.
sources.why_it_matters: Without clear policy content, this source adds little to the Fed reaction-function assessment beyond confirming ongoing Fed communication.

sources.title: U.S. Employment (July 2026)
sources.evidence_text: TD Economics said July payrolls fell 23,000, prior months were revised down, and average hourly earnings growth slowed to 3.2% year over year.
sources.why_it_matters: Downward revisions plus slower wage growth strengthen the case that labor-market momentum is cooling enough to ease policy.

sources.title: Initial Claims (ICSA) | FRED | St. Louis Fed
sources.evidence_text: FRED lists initial claims at 209,000 for the week of 2026-08-08.
sources.why_it_matters: A modest move higher in claims suggests only limited cooling, which is not yet strong enough on its own to force aggressive Fed easing.

sources.title: Weak July jobs report helps case for Fed to hold rates but doesn't take hikes off the table
sources.evidence_text: The July jobs report was weaker than expected and reinforced arguments for the Fed to keep rates unchanged rather than tighten further.
sources.why_it_matters: A softer labor-market print reduces pressure on the Fed to hike and supports a more patient easing stance.

sources.title: July 2026 PCE inflation press coverage of the BEA release
sources.evidence_text: Market coverage emphasized that inflation remained too hot for the Fed to relax policy aggressively.
sources.why_it_matters: If market participants read the PCE report as sticky inflation, that raises the hurdle for additional easing.

sources.title: Fed officials' concerns about inflation sparked talk of rate hike
sources.evidence_text: NBC reported that inflation concerns among Fed officials have revived discussion of a possible rate hike, even though no change was expected at the next meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: Renewed hike discussion signals a more restrictive reaction function, making additional cuts less likely unless inflation data improve.

sources.title: Understanding Fed Funds Futures: Trading, Settling, and Market Expectations
sources.evidence_text: Fed funds futures prices reflect market expectations for future federal funds rate changes and can be translated into expected cuts or hikes.
sources.why_it_matters: If those prices move higher, the implied policy path becomes more restrictive, which is consistent with fewer cuts or more hikes.

sources.title: Treasury Yield Curve Inversions and the Evolution of Monetary Policy Expectations
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
sources.evidence_text: The New York Fed published a staff report discussing how Treasury yields, including the 2-year, embed expectations about the future policy path.
sources.why_it_matters: This supports using the 2-year yield as a reaction-function input because it reflects how markets translate Fed communication and data into expected policy moves.

sources.title: Labor Report First Look
sources.evidence_text: The Atlanta Fed's first look summary says payroll employment and the unemployment rate changed little in July, with payrolls down 23,000 and unemployment at 4.1%.
sources.why_it_matters: Fed watchers use this interpretation as a quick read on whether labor conditions are cooling enough to justify easier policy.

sources.title: ADP National Employment Report - July 2026
sources.evidence_text: ADP reported that private employers added 44,000 jobs in July 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: ADP's private payroll signal is weaker than normal but not as weak as the BLS headline, leaving the Fed with mixed labor-market evidence.

sources.title: Seasonally Adjusted Initial Claims Dashboard
sources.evidence_text: The Labor Department reported seasonally adjusted initial unemployment claims of 209,000 for the week ending August 8, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: Claims near historical low levels argue against an abrupt labor-market deterioration and give the Fed less reason to cut aggressively.

sources.title: CPI Surprises to the Downside
sources.evidence_text: The article says the latest CPI report came in well below expectations, which improved the odds of Fed rate cuts.
sources.why_it_matters: A softer inflation surprise reduces pressure on the Fed to keep policy restrictive and supports additional easing.

sources.title: FOMC statement: Federal Reserve holds rates unchanged at July 29 meeting
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC kept the federal funds target range unchanged and said it would keep assessing incoming data, the outlook, and the balance of risks.
sources.why_it_matters: A hold with data-dependent guidance suggests the Fed is not yet moving decisively toward either easier or tighter policy.

sources.title: FOMC Statement: July 2026
sources.evidence_text: The note says the July FOMC kept the policy rate unchanged and recorded three dissents favoring a hike.
sources.why_it_matters: Dissents for hikes indicate internal pressure toward tighter policy, which can offset market hopes for cuts.

sources.title: US: Fed Chair Press Conference
sources.evidence_text: CME’s note says the July FOMC left the target range unchanged and repeated that it would deliver price stability while inflation stayed elevated.
sources.why_it_matters: Market-facing summaries that emphasize sticky inflation reinforce a higher-for-longer interpretation of the Fed’s reaction function.

sources.title: Fed Minutes and the September Rate-Cut Debate: What Traders Are Pricing
sources.evidence_text: The piece says traders price the chance of a cut through fed funds futures, CME FedWatch, and the 2-year Treasury yield, all of which move with incoming data.
sources.why_it_matters: The 2-year yield and fed funds futures are closely watched because they reflect the market's expected Fed path and therefore the likely stance of policy.

sources.title: Fed rate cut/hike odds & probabilities by meeting
sources.evidence_text: The site shows the next meeting priced with a 49% hike probability and later meetings implying a lower post-meeting rate, including September at about 3.13%.
sources.why_it_matters: If the implied path falls over successive meetings, the market is still looking for eventual easing despite near-term hike risk.
